newsitem.title: FINLAND: WEEK AHEAD - FINNISH STOCKS SEEN CORRECTING LOWER.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - FINNISH STOCKS SEEN CORRECTING LOWER.

text.p: Outlook for Finnish financial markets next week according to economists and analysts:
*Stocks probably in for downward correction,
*Bonds will track German Bunds,
*Markka under pressure to firm, to trade in 2.97-2.99 range,
*Domestic December jobless data to be largely ignored,
*Demand for state treasury T-bills to remain good,
*Bundesbank council meeting, U.S. Fed beige book key international topics
WALL ST. KEY FOR STOCKS, WHICH MAY CORRECT LOWER
U.S. share performance will remain in focus. Finnish shares may be in for a downward correction after recent steep rises.

"The rise cannot continue this strong ... a technical correction (down) is possible next week," said Martti Larjo, analyst at Merita Securities. Since the beginning of January, the HEX index has climbed about nine percent.
Enskilda analyst Johannes Schulman said that if coming earnings reports by foreign telecoms and forestry companies were weaker than expected, corresponding Finnish stocks could be hit.
On Tuesday, Aspo will release preliminary 1996 earnings, and Efore (former Finlandia Interface) will publish its year to end-October earnings.
BOND MARKET TO FOCUS ON GERMANY
The bond market is expected to move in line with German Bunds next week, said Juha Lehtonen, analyst at Merita Bank.
Reactions caused by price changes on the U.S market are expected to be more subdued on the Finnish market, he added.
The Bundesbank will hold its regular council meeting on Thursday. A majority of market operators do not expect any change in German key rates, analysts said.
The U.S. Federal Reserve's FOMC will issue its Beige Book on Wednesday which may give clues for the course of the U.S. economy.
MARKKA UNDER PRESSURE IN 2.97-99 RANGE
Markka buying is expected to continue next week keeping the markka under pressure to appreciate. But the markka is seen remaining in a 2.97-99 range.
Teijo Rantatupa, market analyst at OKOBANK said that "a technical correction in DEM/FIM may take place next week taking that it to a level around 2.99.
It ended on Friday at 2.9785.
Large amounts of markka has recently been bought against other currencies, mainly by overseas investors. The Bank of Finland said it had intervened to halt the strengthening.
GOOD DEMAND FOR T-BILLS SEEN TO CONTINUE
On Tuesday, the State Treasury Office (STO) will hold its regular weekly auction. Analysts expected recent good demand for T-bills to hold. STO will sell 89-day, 180-day and 364-day T-bills.
FINNISH DECEMBER JOBLESS DATA UNINTERESTING
Statistics Finland (SF) will release December unemployment data on Thursday at 0700/0500 GMT. The figure is expected to be ignored by the markets, analysts said.
The Labour Ministry said the jobless rate rose to 19.0 percent in December from 17.4 percent in November. SF's November figure was 15.9 percent. SF data is used in international comparisons.
--Tuula Franck, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 245
